title: Formulas over a structure translate to formulas over its labelled tree at the same quantifier complexity, and back
source_title: Scott sentence complexities of linear orderings

standard_prerequisites.name: Labelled tree of a structure
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every structure A has a labelled tree T_A of finite tuples ordered by extension, and for every tuple a in A there is a node sigma of T_A above it.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the object the two translations go between.

standard_prerequisites.name: Infinitary formulas of bounded rank
standard_prerequisites.statement: P_alpha and the classes Gamma^in_alpha are the infinitary formulas of quantifier rank below alpha built with the corresponding operations.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the classes the two directions preserve.

standard_prerequisites.name: Turing computable embedding
standard_prerequisites.statement: A Turing computable embedding from a class of structures with parameters into labelled trees with parameters, extending the parameter-free Friedman-Stanley embedding.
standard_prerequisites.use: It carries the pull-back direction of the proof.

core_obligations: For the push-forward direction, translate quantifier-free formulas by putting them in disjunctive normal form and reading off, for each disjunct, the height condition on the node and the containment of the disjunct in its label (source lines 251-258).

Handle the existential step by taking T_psi to be the formula saying that some successor node satisfies T_phi, and note that the limit case is immediate, which closes the induction on quantifier rank (source lines 259-265).

For the pull-back direction, fix a tuple of nodes and construct the parameterised embedding Psi_sigma by non-uniformly partitioning the parameters and taking the lexicographically least finite tuples whose subtrees are isomorphic to those described by sigma (source lines 267-281).
Apply the pull-back theorem for that embedding and use that its image contains the parameterised tree of the fixed tuple, which gives the same-complexity formula psi* (source lines 281-285).

proof_roadmap.step: Quantifier-free base case by disjunctive normal form.
Existential and limit steps, closing the push-forward direction.
Build the parameterised Turing computable embedding for the pull-back direction.
Apply the pull-back theorem along that embedding.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source0.tex lines 234-249: for every structure A and every infinitary formula over its vocabulary there is a formula of the same quantifier rank over the labelled tree of A that holds at every node above a tuple exactly when the original holds at that tuple, and conversely every formula over the tree has an equivalent formula over A of the same rank. The statement contains no construction, and the proof (source lines 250-286) has to build both directions: the push-forward direction by disjunctive normal form for the quantifier-free case, then an induction whose existential step replaces a quantifier by a quantifier over successor nodes, with the height and label conditions read off the tree; the pull-back direction is a different kind of argument, constructing a parameterised Turing computable embedding by choosing, for a fixed tuple of nodes, the lexicographically least finite tuples whose subtrees are isomorphic to the ones described by that tuple, and then invoking the pull-back theorem along it. Neither the disjunctive normal form reduction nor the embedding construction is visible in the statement.
